jobs.description:
Title:
Deputy Operations Manager

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

Around here, we define the future.

We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers. But we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

The Department of Defense (DoD) developed the Military and Family Life Counseling (MFLC) program as an initiative of the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Military Community and Family Policy (MC&FP), facilitating private and confidential Non-Medical Counseling services.

The MFLC Program was established to expand access to confidential, face-to-face counseling and reduce the barriers and stigma often associated with seeking counseling support.
Currently, the MFLC Program provides non-medical counseling, consultation, and outreach services to more than 200 military installations or nearby civilian communities located in most all the 50 states, the District of Columbia, United States (U.S.) territories and commonwealths, and over 25 foreign countries including areas considered hazardous duty/danger zones.

POSITION IS CONTINGENT UPON CONTRACT AWARD.

Position is remote. Part-Time, less than 20 hours per week until award decision is made, if KBR is awarded the contract, position becomes full-time.

KBR is seeking a Deputy Operations Manager.  This position will report to the Operations Manager and shall be a part of the management team. Responsibilities will include overseeing the human resources duties and managing the daily operations of the contract. Deputy will partner with the Operations Manager ensuring that Government worldwide assignment requests, currently provided via TDLs, are fulfilled in a timely manner and execution of all work assignment logistics and travel, to meet assignments, are completed and coordinated with the applicable stakeholders’ POCs per worksite. Shall ensure efficient and effective operational procedures and processes to enable successful contract execution, as well as quality of services delivery to eligible participants.

Qualifications:
a. At least five years of experience managing program operations for an international,
globally dynamic, geographically dispersed, rapidly changing, and diverse program environment.
b. At least five years of experience with human resource management and worksite/assignment tracking, financial management, and stakeholder communications.

Desired Qualifications:
BS / BA Engineering, Sciences, or a related field
a. At least two years’ experience managing SLAs under an incentive-based contract.
b. At least two years’ experience supporting military organizations.
c. A bachelor’s degree, at a minimum, from an accredited university or college in business administration, project management, and/or similar academic profession

jobs.description:
Title:
Contract Program Manager

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?
- Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
- Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
- Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

This is a contingent position based upon contract award

KBR is seeking an Expert-Level Contract Program Manager (CPM) to support a procurement providing Systems Engineering and Integration (SE&I) support to an IC/DOD government customer within the Washington DC Metropolitan area.
The CPM will be the interface with the government customer regarding contract activities and programmatic, and overall contract or program performance. To achieve this, the CPM shall maintain regular communication with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) and Government Program Manager (PM), keeping them informed of relevant contractor related information especially significant risks and issues and the associated resolution plans and status.
The CPM will be responsible for day-to-day contract activities to include formulating and enforcing work deliverables, assigning schedules, reviewing work discrepancies, supervising contractor personnel and communicating policies objectives and goals of the organization to the contractor team. The CPM will also help establish both technical and business goals in consultation with top management and make detailed plans for the accomplishment of the established goals.

Primary Responsibilities:
- Ensuring the timely execution of all financial, staffing and administrative contract actions.
- Lead the team assisting the customer in the development, implementation, and adoption of the Digital Engineering (DE) environment, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) practices, and Digital Twin capabilities
- Serve as the primary point of contact with the government customer and key figures and offices (including the Chief Engineer and Program Executive Offices (PEOs)) within the organization.
- Provide contract management support to the Program(s) PMO to ensure the timely execution of all financial, staffing and administrative contract actions.
- Provide program management support to include cost, schedule, risk and performance management of all staff and work activities.
- Ensure contractor personnel are qualified to perform the assigned task and that potential personnel problems are pre-empted.
- Ensure contract tasks are completed within the specified timelines.
- Establish and implement processes and procedures enabling the rapid response to surge requirements for increased contract personnel.
- Ensure programmatic alignment and adherence to the customer’s visions and priorities.
- Ensure the accuracy, quality, configuration management and timely delivery of all required deliverables to include the Monthly Financial Report, Monthly Staffing Report, Monthly Activity Report, Quarterly Program Management Review materials, and as required Trip Reports, Briefings, Evaluations, Technical Assignments, White Papers or other Government requested deliverables necessary for the successful execution and/or completion of work activities.
- Plan and execute Quarterly Program Reviews to provide the Government customer(s) an comprehensive understanding of the health/status of all activities.
- Coordination program management activities between various offices within the customer organization.
-  Perform day-to-day contractual and programmatic management of the TO.
- Monitor performance metrics, SLAs, and KPIs and report progress to government customer leadership

Required Qualifications:
- Master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, Management Information Systems, or related STEM degree program, or equivalent Expert level experience as a Program Manager.
- Expert-level experience (10 years or more) as a Program Manager in terms of managing program level cost, schedule, performance, and risk management for a development, engineering, or other Information Technology DoD or IC program.
- Project Management Professional (PMP), DAWIA Level III certification in Program Management, or similar professional certification in program management or demonstrated experience applying Project Management tools and techniques.
- Extensive experience working with Customer, and other IC\DoD mission partners.
- Ability to engage with senior government stakeholders and lead cross-functional teams.
- Expert experience as a Program Manager in terms of cost, schedule, performance, and risk management.
- Demonstrated experience in engineering, Enterprise engineering, design and analysis of IT or related systems experience in all phases of design, development, analysis and documentation, and development of standards and guidelines for tasks being performed.
- Expert-level working experience in government or industry in DoD/IC Acquisition Process or PPBES.
- Active TS/SCI required
- Experience with Digital Engineering (DE) and Model Based System Engineering (MBSE)

Desired Skills and Experience:
- Knowledge of the geospatial intelligence mission and its contributions to the Intelligence Community.
- Knowledge of the National System for Geospatial Intelligence.
- Working knowledge of Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), processes, tools and languages.
- Experience with the development and/or review of cost estimates and the associated technical work scope necessary to achieve stated objectives.
- Experience in tailoring and using both Agile and Waterfall development methodologies
- Experience with the identification of technical issues and proactive communication of possible impacts.
- Experience in performing validation and verification of various engineering results and deliverables to ensure the highest quality results against customer requirements.
- Experience advising and assisting the government leadership team in achieving their mission objectives by leveraging the combine resources within the government team and their industrial base
- Basic understanding of cloud technologies, DevSecOps, CI/CD pipelines, and AI/ML integration.

Basic Compensation:
$177,300 - $216,600
This range is for the Virginia area only

The offered rate will be based on the selected candidate’s knowledge, skills, abilities and/or experience and in consideration of internal parity.

Additional Compensation:
KBR may offer bonuses, commissions, or other forms of compensation to certain job titles or levels, per internal policy or contractual designation. Additional compensation may be in the form of sign on bonus, relocation benefits, short-term incentives, long-term incentives, or discretionary payments for exceptional performance.

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Title:
Program Manager

Who We Are
KBR Government Solutions delivers full life cycle professional and technical solutions that improve operational readiness and drive innovation. Our solutions help ensure mission success on land, air, sea, space and cyberspace for the Department of Defense, Intelligence Community, NASA and other federal agencies. KBR’s areas of expertise include engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity.  KBR strives to create a safer, more secure and sustainable world by bringing together the best and brightest to deliver technologies and solutions that help our customers accomplish their most critical missions and objectives.

The Mission Ahead
This role is with KBR’s Government Solutions U.S. division.  At KBR Government Solutions, we don't just envision a world that's safer, more secure, and sustainable - we create it. Our legacy of delivering advanced full life cycle professional and technical solutions is matched only by our commitment to operational readiness and innovation. As stewards of critical missions for the Department of Defense, Intelligence Community, NASA, and other key federal entities, we excel in engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT, and cybersecurity. United in our quest for excellence, KBR stands at the vanguard, ready to transform possibilities into impactful realities for a better tomorrow.

Who You Are
A forward-looking leader, you stay abreast of industry and academic trends in program management, applying advanced tools and practices to your work. You possess a solid foundation in business concepts and accounting principles necessary for meticulous project cost and budgetary oversight. Your role often involves strategic interface with business unit Controllers and Marketing teams, leveraging opportunities and managing business pursuits with informed judgement. An in-depth understanding of all facets of facilities management, and business operations is fundamental to your role, as is extensive experience in program management and progressive leadership responsibility. Your qualifications may also be matched by substantial professional experience in lieu of formal education.

Operations run 24x7 therefore your responsibilities extend beyond traditional boundaries to ensure continuous availability of critical systems and the facilities’ infrastructure while maintaining exceptional appearance and first-class maintenance of facilities to provide outstanding customer service to high-level dignitaries and senior executive stakeholders.

An adept leader, you're no stranger to navigating large-scale projects with finesse. Your expertise in resource management, strategic planning, and process improvement is surpassed only by your commitment to balancing stakeholder expectations with concrete business outcomes. Your eye for compliance and your strategic mindset ensures that each contractual requirement is not just met but exceeded. As a navigator of complexity, you are prepared to architect the integration of project data, optimize resource allocation, and achieve operational excellence across the board.

This role will be located in Alice Springs, Australia at a 4,400-acre facility with approximately 687,000 square feet of mission and support space.  The Program Manager will be expected to travel between our facilities in Alice Springs and the local area.   This position is expected to be onsite 100% and is contingent upon contract award.

What You’ll Do
As a Program Manager (PM), you will:
- Experience working in 24x7 mission-critical environments supporting facilities construction, operations, and maintenance, and support services where continuous availability of facility infrastructure is essential and of the highest priority

- Display strong technical, programmatic and personal leadership skills

- Knowledgeable of the guidelines provided by the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR)

- Professional certification such as PMP, CFM, PE, FAC-P/PM Mid-Level, or Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) Level 2 certification in Program Management

- Responsible for the execution of the SOW within the cost and on schedule to include but not limited to: Ensuring community of support during Contractor personnel change; Interfacing Contractor Officer (CO), COTR, and Chief of Facilities; Delivery of all contract requirements; Managing subcontracts and be responsible for the performance and conduct of subcontractor personnel

- Strategic Oversight: Command the planning, resourcing, and execution across multiple programs/projects, ensuring alignment with business and product line strategies

- Financial Stewardship: Scrutinize and sanction financial frameworks and reports, maintaining the integrity of management reserves and expenditure

- Holistic Integration: Champion cross-functional team efforts to deliver a synchronized service that addresses every angle of the Government's requirements

- Risk Management: Strategize and allocate funds for risk mitigation, safeguarding project outcomes

- Communication: Communicate effectively with all customers, and maintain a transparent and proactive dialogue with the Government, ensuring clarity and prompt resolution of issues

- Customer Service: Demonstrate strong customer service skills

- Regulatory Adherence: Vigilantly enforce all contractual, regulatory, and compliance mandates in partnership with the contracts team

- Possess an active TS/SCI U.S. Security Clearance with Counterintelligence polygraph or host nation PV clearance

- A minimum of 10 years of prior relevant PM and Intelligence Community (IC) experience managing a large (250+ person) multi-disciplinary workforce including tradesmen, engineers, warehousing personnel, and other base operating support staff

Preferred Qualifications
- 10 years of experience in formal management, leading a team

- 5 years of experience working with business strategy

- 5 years of experience developing project execution plans, schedules, and budgets

- 5 years of experience supporting the Federal and/or Intelligence Community

- 5 years of experience with long range business plans

- Experience building and sustaining high performing integrated teams

- Knowledge of process improvement models (e.g. LEAN/Six Sigma, ISO 9000)

- Proficient knowledge and experience in the use of project management concepts to manage items including, but not limited to: project schedule, scope, cost, risk, and deliverables and related metrics

- Experience planning and implementing large-scale facility and logistics projects

- Knowledge of U.S. government exercise or crisis management communities and experience planning, coordinating and executing support to special events

- Familiarity with 24/7/365 operational environment

Ready to Make a Difference?
If you’re excited about making a significant impact in the field of space defense and working on projects that matter, we encourage you to apply and join our team at KBR. Let's shape the future together.

jobs.description:
Title:
Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Analyst

The Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Analyst plays a critical role in driving financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, performance reporting, and strategic decision support. This highly visible position partners closely with finance leaders and business stakeholders to deliver actionable insights, evaluate business performance, and influence key operational and strategic decisions. The role supports the annual budgeting process, periodic forecasts, long-range planning activities, and management reporting while helping shape the financial foundation of a newly independent public company. The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and financial modeling capabilities with intellectual curiosity, business acumen, and the ability to translate complex financial data into meaningful recommendations that drive performance and growth.

This role will support a strategic business unit while partnering closely with the Corporate FP&A organization to drive planning, forecasting, performance reporting, and decision support across the enterprise. Opportunities exist to support either Exploration and Logistics (E&L), which delivers global mission operations, space exploration, engineering, and logistics solutions, or Defense and Intel (D&I), which provides mission-critical capabilities across complex defense, intelligence, and classified environments.

Trinzic is being established as an independent public company through the planned separation of KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business, which is expected to be completed on January 4, 2027. This role offers a rare opportunity to join the organization during a pivotal period of growth and transformation, helping establish and mature the financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and performance management capabilities of a newly independent public company while supporting critical government and commercial missions around the world.

Key Responsibilities
- Support the annual budgeting process, including preparation, consolidation, analysis, and reporting for corporate functions and business initiatives.

- Develop and maintain short- and long-term financial forecasts, leveraging financial models and business assumptions to support planning activities.

- Perform monthly and quarterly variance analyses comparing actual results to budget and forecast, identifying key drivers, trends, risks, and opportunities.

- Partner with business leaders, department budget owners, and cross-functional stakeholders to develop budgets, evaluate financial performance, and provide actionable recommendations.

- Prepare executive-level financial reports, dashboards, and presentations that communicate business performance, highlight emerging trends, and support strategic decision-making by senior leadership.

- Assist in the development and enhancement of financial models, planning tools, and reporting processes to improve forecasting accuracy and operational efficiency.

- Support month-end and quarter-end financial review activities, ensuring data accuracy and timely analysis of results.

- Contribute to the preparation of Annual Operating Plans (AOP), periodic forecasts, long-range plans, and strategic financial analyses.

- Evaluate financial performance against established targets and assist in identifying corrective actions to address budget variances and improve business outcomes.

- Serve as a trusted finance partner to Accounting and business stakeholders, ensuring alignment between financial plans, forecasts, operating performance, and strategic objectives.

- Identify opportunities to improve financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting processes through automation, standardization, and best practices.

- Assist in evaluating business performance through trend analysis, scenario modeling, and key performance indicators (KPIs), providing insights that support enterprise planning and value creation initiatives.

- Lead and support financial analyses, business cases, and scenario modeling efforts that evaluate strategic initiatives, resource allocations, investments, and growth opportunities.

Basic Qualifications
Education & Experience
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.

- 5+ years of experience in financial planning and analysis, corporate finance, accounting, consulting, investment banking, or a related financial discipline.

- Experience supporting annual budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes within a corporate FP&A or related finance environment.

- Strong understanding of financial statements, including income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements.

- Experience presenting financial analyses and recommendations to management and business stakeholders.

Technical & Leadership Skills
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including complex financial models, scenario analysis, and data manipulation.

- Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.

- Experience with ERP, financial planning, and reporting systems.

- Ability to synthesize large data sets and communicate insights effectively to both finance and non-finance audiences.

- Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.

- Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

- High attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

- Ability to work independently while effectively collaborating across functions and levels of the organization.

Preferred Qualifications
- MBA or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or Business Administration.

- CPA, CMA, CFA, or progress toward a professional finance certification.

- Demonstrated experience leading or supporting complex budgeting and forecasting processes and delivering actionable financial insights to business stakeholders.

- Experience supporting a publicly traded company.

- Experience within government contracting, aerospace, defense, engineering, technology, or professional services industries.

- Experience supporting investor relations, board reporting, or SEC-related financial analysis.

- Experience with financial planning platforms such as Anaplan, Workday Adaptive Planning, Oracle EPM, Hyperion, or similar tools.

- Experience with business intelligence and data visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau.

Title:

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced finance professional to take ownership of financial reporting, governance, statutory compliance, and internal controls within a complex and dynamic business environment. This role plays a critical part in ensuring the integrity of the general ledger, maintaining compliance with relevant regulations, and delivering accurate and timely financial information to support business decision-making.

As a key member of the finance team, you will be responsible for ensuring that all financial information reported to Corporate, external auditors, and regulatory bodies is complete, accurate, and fully compliant with US GAAP, IFRS, and UK GAAP. Why Join Us?

This is an exciting opportunity to join KBR during a period of significant transformation. Following the announced spin-off of KBR's Government Solutions business into Trinzic , you will play a key role in supporting the business through this transition while helping to shape the future finance function. The spin-off creates unique opportunities for professional growth, increased responsibility, and long-term career development within a newly independent organisation.

This is an exciting time to join KBR as the company prepares for the forthcoming spin-off of its Government Solutions business into Trinzic, creating new opportunities for growth, transformation, and career development.

jobs.title: Global Network, Voice and Audiovisual Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Title:
Global Network, Voice and Audiovisual Operations Manager

About the Role
The Global Network, Voice and Audiovisual Operations Manager will lead a geographically distributed team responsible for enterprise LAN, WAN, wireless, internet, data centre networking, voice, unified communications, video conferencing and audiovisual services.

The role supports corporate offices, project locations, data centres, remote sites and restricted operating environments across multiple regions and time zones.

Reporting to the Director, Networks and Infrastructure, the successful candidate will be accountable for service availability, performance, capacity, security, resilience, lifecycle management, operational support and continuous improvement across the assigned portfolio.

Key Responsibilities
• Lead, develop and hold accountable a global team responsible for network, voice, unified communications, conferencing and audiovisual services.
• Oversee enterprise LAN, WAN, wireless, internet, data centre network and remote site connectivity services.

• Manage the operation and lifecycle of routers, switches, wireless infrastructure, software defined WAN platforms, network controllers and associated management technologies.

• Oversee data centre network services, including leaf and spine architectures, VXLAN, EVPN, routing, segmentation and high availability.
• Maintain reliable connectivity between data centres, offices, business partners, customer locations and remote sites.

• Oversee foundational network services within the assigned scope, including DNS, DHCP, IP address management and network time services.
• Partner with Cybersecurity on firewalls, secure remote access, network access control, VPN and secure access services.

• Lead enterprise voice and telecommunications services, including Microsoft Teams Phone or comparable platforms, SIP services, carriers, telephone numbers, voicemail and emergency calling.

• Oversee enterprise meeting room and audiovisual services, including conference rooms, boardrooms, training spaces, video conferencing, digital signage and room control systems.

• Establish operational standards, support models and technology profiles for different meeting room and audiovisual requirements.

• Maintain effective capacity, performance and service health reporting covering availability, latency, packet loss, wireless coverage, call quality and conferencing reliability.

• Lead the response to major network, voice and audiovisual incidents, ensuring effective recovery, communication, root cause analysis and corrective action.

• Manage carriers, circuit providers, audiovisual integrators, manufacturers and managed service providers.

• Support operating budgets, capital planning, telecommunications expenditure, licensing, renewals and cost optimisation.

• Provide operational leadership for carrier migrations, office openings and closures, data centre activity, acquisitions, divestitures and enterprise separation programmes.

About You
You will have substantial experience managing enterprise network and communications services within a large, complex or regulated organisation.

You should also demonstrate:
• Experience leading geographically distributed infrastructure teams.
• Strong knowledge of enterprise routing, switching, wireless networking, WAN, internet and data centre networking.
• Experience with technologies such as Cisco Catalyst, Cisco Nexus and Cisco Meraki, or comparable enterprise platforms.
• Experience with SD-WAN, carrier networks, BGP, OSPF, MPLS, VPN, quality of service, DNS, DHCP and IP address management.
• Experience with Microsoft Teams Phone, Cisco collaboration technologies or comparable voice and conferencing platforms.
• Experience managing telecommunications carriers, circuit providers and audiovisual service partners.
• An understanding of enterprise audiovisual technologies, meeting room standards and operational support models.
• Strong IT service management, major incident, problem management and operational risk capabilities.
• Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain service risks and investment requirements to senior stakeholders.
Experience within engineering, government services, aerospace, defence or another highly regulated sector would be advantageous. Relevant Cisco, Microsoft, ITIL or audiovisual certifications are also desirable.

Location
United Kingdom, based at the company’s Leatherhead Campus , with hybrid working in accordance with KBR’s applicable policy.

The role supports global services across multiple regions and time zones.

Regular UK travel and occasional international travel will be required.

The successful candidate must have the right to work in the United Kingdom and may be required to obtain and maintain an appropriate level of security clearance.

KBR Company Information

When you become part of the KBR team, your opportunities are endless. Through collaboration with our customers, we’re defining tomorrow’s challenges, then providing the solutions and services to overcome those challenges, always maintaining our commitment to total safety and reliability.

At KBR, we partner with government and industry clients to provide purposeful and comprehensive solutions with an emphasis on efficiency and safety. With a full portfolio of services, proprietary technologies and expertise, our employees are ready to handle projects and missions throughout their entire lifecycle, from planning and design to sustainability and maintenance. Whether at the bottom of the ocean or in outer space, our clients trust us to deliver the impossible on a daily basis.

Working at KBR means being rewarded for your contributions. In addition to competitive benefits and professional development, our people are empowered to use all their potential, creating meaningful change for themselves and our clients. We attract the best minds in the world because our expertise thrives on creativity, resourcefulness and collaboration. That is how we supply our clients with cutting-edge solutions and services.

Title:

THIS POSITION IS LOCATED IN JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA

Program Summary

The Marine Corps Prepositioning Program (MCPP) is based in Jacksonville, Florida. We provide maintenance and logistic services to the U.S. Marine Corps (USMC) in support of this program. For over 35 years we have planned, coordinated, and executed the maintenance and logistic services for ground combat vehicles and support equipment for USMC Expeditionary Forces.

Job Summary

The Ashore Operations Manager is responsible for overseeing international ashore-based site task orders involving maintenance and supply services for United States Marine Corps (USMC) tactical equipment.   This role involves overseeing logistics services, supply chain management, distribution management, and maintenance of Marine Corps Prepositioning Program (MCPP) assets staged outside of the continental United States and includes contracting, budgeting, policy, procedural, and personnel support. The Overseas Operations Manager will ensure all operations function in accordance with the contract statement of work and can be performed during times of crisis, maintaining high standards of security and accountability for sensitive equipment.
- Lead, coordinate, and manage the accountability, readiness, and sustainment of overseas prepositioning sites.

- Plan, develop, and maintain a competent and complete program that follows the contract Statement of Work and adheres to Marine Corps policy and procedures.

- Coordinate Task Order deliverables in support of MCPP planning and execution requirements.

- Oversee and coordinate support for customer requests over and above the scope of the Task Order.

- Oversee the money, manpower, materiel, facilities, and services needed to support overseas prepositioning sites.

- Oversee and manage the budget execution for overseas prepositioning sites.

Title:

The PM provides strategic oversight of training operations, instructor workforce management, curriculum development, quality assurance, contract compliance, and customer relations while ensuring the successful delivery of operational C-UAS training at multiple CONUS and OCONUS locations.

The PM serves as the primary point of contact for Government customers, Contracting Officers, Contracting Officer Representatives (CORs), and supported military organizations. Job Summary
The Deputy Program Manager (DPM) serves as the principal deputy to the Program Manager and provides direct support in the execution, oversight, and management of all contract performance under the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Public Assistance Technical Assistance Contract (PA TAC VI). The DPM assists in providing leadership, operational direction, quality management, and administrative oversight to ensure the successful delivery of technical, programmatic, and administrative support services in support of FEMA's Public Assistance Program and disaster recovery mission.
The DPM supports the planning, organization, coordination, and execution of all contract activities, resources, personnel, subcontractors, and deliverables while ensuring compliance with contract requirements, FEMA policies, federal regulations, and applicable performance standards. The DPM helps manage a geographically dispersed workforce supporting multiple concurrent disasters nationwide and contributes to rapid mobilization, scalable operations, and continuous mission readiness.

The DPM serves as the designated alternate to the Program Manager and assumes responsibility for program operations during the Program Manager's absence. This position requires the ability to support nationwide disaster operations, including periodic travel and availability during emergency activation periods.

The DPM assists with day-to-day contract execution across all task orders and disaster assignments, supporting nationwide surge operations and disaster deployment activities. Responsibilities include coordinating staffing, resource allocation, deployment readiness, and workload balancing to support multiple simultaneous disaster operations. The DPM ensures timely mobilization, deployment, tracking, and demobilization of personnel and must possess demonstrated experience supporting FEMA programs or similarly complex federal programs.

The DPM supports the Program Manager in ensuring contract performance meets or exceeds all performance metrics, service level requirements, and quality standards. The DPM contributes to program governance activities, including performance assessments, risk management, quality reviews, corrective action implementation, and continuous improvement initiatives while supporting overall cost, schedule, and performance objectives.

This role requires an experienced, adaptable leader capable of operating in austere and rapidly changing environments while maintaining strict compliance with contractual, safety, and quality standards. The DPM will promote KBR's Zero Harm culture and ensure operations are executed in accordance with company policies, applicable regulations, and customer requirements.

Please Note: This role is contingent upon final project approval and contract funding.

- Federal Program and Project Management

- FEMA Public Assistance Expertise

- Disaster Recovery Operations

- Stakeholder Engagement

- Quality Assurance and Continuous Improvement

- Risk Management

- Workforce Planning and Resource Coordination

- Contract Administration

- Strategic Communications

The PM provides executive leadership, strategic direction, operational oversight, and quality management to ensure the successful delivery of technical, programmatic, and administrative support services in support of FEMA's Public Assistance Program and disaster recovery mission.

The PM is responsible for planning, organizing, directing, coordinating, and controlling all contract activities, resources, personnel, subcontractors, and deliverables while ensuring compliance with contract requirements, FEMA policies, federal regulations, and applicable performance standards. The PM leads a geographically dispersed workforce capable of supporting multiple concurrent disasters nationwide and ensures rapid mobilization, scalable operations, and continuous mission readiness.  This position requires the ability to support nationwide disaster operations, including periodic travel and availability during emergency activation periods.  In addition, Direct day-to-day contract execution across all task orders and disaster assignments and managing nationwide surge operations and disaster deployment activities which includes: coordinating staffing, resource allocation, and workload balancing to support multiple simultaneous disaster operations. While ensuring timely mobilization, deployment, tracking, and demobilization of personnel, the PM must have sound PM skills and capabilities demonstrated by supporting other FEMA programs or similar complex programs.

The PM will ensure contract performance meets or exceeds all performance metrics, service level requirements, and quality standards and leads program governance activities, including executive reviews, performance assessments, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives. While maintaining responsibility for overall contract cost, schedule, and performance.

Please Note: This role is contingent upon final project approval and contract funding.

Core Competencies
- Strategic Leadership

- Federal Program Management

- FEMA Public Assistance Expertise

- Disaster Recovery Operations

- Stakeholder Management

- Quality Assurance and Continuous Improvement

- Risk Management

- Resource Planning and Workforce Management

- Financial and Contract Management

- Executive Communication

- Problem Solving and Decision Making

- Mission-Focused Service Delivery

The Program Manager shall demonstrate:
- Comprehensive knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance Program delivery, grant management, and disaster recovery operations.

- Experience applying Stafford Act authorities, 2 CFR Part 200, FEMA Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG), and applicable federal regulations.

- Experience managing large-scale disaster recovery operations involving multiple simultaneous federally declared disasters.

- Training and experience in Incident Command System (ICS) principles and emergency management operations.

- Experience overseeing geographically dispersed teams supporting field, regional, and headquarters operations.

- Familiarity with FEMA's recovery mission, state and local government coordination, and stakeholder engagement processes.

This role requires an experienced, forward-leaning leader capable of operating in austere, rapidly changing environments while maintaining strict compliance with contractual, safety, and quality standards. The PM will enforce KBR’s Zero Harm culture and ensure all operations are executed in accordance with company policies, applicable regulations, and customer requirements

Roles and Responsibilities
- Lead the contract and task orders with day-to-day execution of program operations, ensuring sustainment goals, strategic objectives, financial goals, and customer expectations are met or exceeded.

- Liaison between key stakeholders to ensure efficient delivery and proactive risk management.

- Plan and support execution of End-Use Monitoring (EUM) activities, including in-person, secondary, and virtual monitoring inspections in Ukraine.

- Design and implement monitoring tools and program surveys, including sampling plans, tool development, and digital data collection methods.

- Lead field supervision efforts to generate high-quality evidence on program performance and outcomes.

- Oversee data cleaning, validation, and analysis to ensure structure, accuracy, integrity, and readiness for internal decision-making and external reporting.

- Prepare clear, funder-ready analytical reports and professional data visualizations that translate complex findings into actionable insights and demonstrate results against agreed indicators and targets.

- Oversee and manage a team of contractor personnel technically proficient in monitoring and evaluation activities and possess the requisite property management and related experience necessary for EUM.

- Maintain accurate documentation and reporting processes, including Excel-based tracking, inventory support (as applicable), and compliance-ready program records.

Highly Desired:

- FEMA National Incident Management System (NIMS) training:
- IS-100: Introduction to Incident Command System (ICS)

- IS-200: Basic Incident Command System for Initial Response

- IS-700: National Incident Management System, An Introduction

- IS-800: National Response Framework, An Introduction

- FEMA-approved cybersecurity and information security awareness training as required for access to FEMA systems and data.

- FEMA records management, privacy, and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) training as required under contract requirements.

Preferred Certifications:

The following certifications are highly desirable:
- Program Management Professional (PMP)

- Certified Emergency Manager (CEM)

- Associate Emergency Manager (AEM)

- FEMA Professional Development Series (PDS)

- FEMA Advanced Professional Series (APS)

- Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt

- Certified Construction Manager (CCM)

- Professional Engineer (PE)

- Certified Floodplain Manager (CFM)

- PMI Risk Management Professional (PMI-RMP)

Continuing Education Requirements
The Program Manager shall maintain professional certifications and complete all FEMA-required training throughout the life of the contract. The Program Manager is expected to participate in periodic FEMA updates, policy implementation training, readiness exercises, and disaster workforce development activities to ensure continued proficiency in Public Assistance delivery and disaster recovery operations.

- Must have a minimum of a bachelor’s degree in business or a related technical field such as program assessment and technical assistance on FEMA programs

- Must also have a minimum of 15 years of experience performing program management functions. This experience must include previous experience as a Program Manager on multiple projects of comparable magnitude and complexity of this contract.

- Should have disaster operational experience

- Should have Project Management Professional (PMP) certification

- Must have high-level management and leadership skills

- Ability to both lead and function as a member of a team.

- Should have excellent written and oral communication skills

- Must have attention to detail, great organizational skills, as well as the ability to multi-task and work well under pressure.

- Must have conflict resolution and problem-solving skills to include risk management

- Must have cost control and budgeting skills

- Must have teamwork and motivational skills

- Bachelor’s degree in Program Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

- Expertise in KPI reporting, risk management integration, and formal change control processes

- Strong understanding of FEMA technical assistance programs and requires rules, regulations, standards, and training

- Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and rapidly changing requirements.

- Ability to maintain high standards of compliance, safety, and quality in dynamic environments.

- U.S. citizenship.

- Ability to deploy and operate in remote or austere locations.

Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelors degree, a Master’s degree is preferred

jobs.description:
Title:
Program Manager – AOC Falconer Modernization

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?
- Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.

- Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.

- Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Position Summary:
KBR is seeking a senior Program Manager to lead a large, mission-critical Air Operations Center (AOC) modernization and sustainment effort. Prior to award, the Program Manager will support capture, proposal, and transition planning activities to ensure KBR develops an executable, mission-focused solution. Following award, the Program Manager will assume overall responsibility for program execution, including customer engagement, technical performance, cost, schedule, staffing, subcontractor management, risk management, and delivery of mission outcomes.  This is a mission-facing leadership role requiring a proven leader who can build trusted relationships with government stakeholders, operators, and teammates while successfully delivering complex operational and technical programs.
The ideal candidate is a former senior AOC, air operations, or operational C2 leader who understands how an AOC actually functions under real mission tempo. This person must understand how government programs are run from the government side: cost, schedule, performance, risk, requirements, stakeholder alignment, contractor accountability, operational readiness, and the realities of fielded weapon system sustainment.  The candidate will exhibit collaborative leadership with the government program office, operators, teammates, and the requirements community.

Key Responsibilities

1. Mission-Facing Program Leadership
·          Lead KBR's Falconer/AOC program strategy and execution activities, ensuring alignment between customer objectives, operational needs, and program performance.
·          Apply firsthand understanding of AOC operations, command relationships, ATO cycles, operational readiness, mission assurance, continuity of operations, and distributed command-and-control requirements.
·          Evaluate proposed technical and programmatic approaches to ensure they are operationally practical and support mission execution.
·          Build and maintain trusted relationships with government stakeholders, operational users, teammates, and internal leadership.
2. Government Program Management Insight
·          Apply extensive program management experience to drive successful execution of cost, schedule, performance, and risk objectives.
·          Develop and implement program management processes, governance structures, staffing plans, reporting mechanisms, and performance metrics.
·          Establish program priorities, monitor program health, and proactively address risks, issues, and dependencies.
·          Ensure all program activities align with customer expectations, contractual requirements, and mission outcomes.
3. Capture and Proposal Support
- Support KBR’s pre-RFP and proposal readiness activities by helping translate mission requirements into clear execution concepts and proposal language.
- Contribute to win themes, discriminators, program management approach, transition strategy, staffing approach, performance objectives, and customer engagement strategy.
- Help prepare for site visits, one-on-one engagements, technical interchange meetings, oral presentations, and executive reviews.
- Coordinate with the Technical Lead, capture leadership, pricing, contracts, BD, operations, and SMEs to ensure the proposed program approach is integrated and credible.

4. Transition and Execution Readiness
- Develop a realistic approach for transitioning from incumbent or current-state operations into KBR-led execution without disrupting mission operations.
- Ensure the program approach addresses 24/7/365 sustainment, help desk, incident escalation, operational availability, training, cyber compliance, and staffing stability.
- If awarded, potentially serve as or support the transition into Program Manager, Senior Advisor, or customer-facing mission lead role.

5. Program Execution
- Assume full responsibility for program execution following contract award, including delivery of technical, operational, and business objectives.
- Manage cost, schedule, performance, staffing, subcontractor execution, and customer satisfaction across the program lifecycle.
- Serve as the primary interface between KBR and government leadership, maintaining strong relationships with program office personnel, operational stakeholders, and requirements owners.
- Lead integrated program reviews, status meetings, risk reviews, and executive-level customer engagements.
- Develop and maintain program plans, staffing plans, financial forecasts, and performance metrics to ensure successful execution.
- Recruit, develop, mentor, and lead a high-performing team of program managers, engineers, operators, and support personnel.
- Monitor program financial performance, including revenue, funding, labor utilization, subcontractor performance, and profitability objectives.
- Identify and mitigate technical, schedule, staffing, operational, and contractual risks before they impact program execution.
- Coordinate closely with the Technical Lead to ensure technical solutions are delivered within cost, schedule, and performance constraints.
- Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and mission focus across the program team.

Work Environment:
- Location: Onsite-Hanscomb AFB-preferred
- Travel Requirements: Up to 25%, with potential travel for customer engagements, industry events, proposal activities, site visits, and transition planning.
- Working Hours: Standard with flexibility required during proposal surge periods and technical review cycles.

Qualifications:
Required:
- Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; advanced military education, graduate degree, or equivalent senior operational leadership experience preferred.
- 15+ years of relevant Air Force, Joint, DoD, or national security experience, including senior leadership in operational command-and-control, air operations, or mission-critical weapon system environments.
- Prior experience leading, managing, or governing large, complex programs, with demonstrated responsibility for cost, schedule, performance, risk management, stakeholder engagement, requirements management, staffing, and operational readiness.
- Demonstrated experience briefing senior military, civilian, and industry leaders.
- Practical understanding of AOC operations, air tasking processes, operational C2, mission assurance, and the constraints of maintaining live operational systems.
- Ability to lead cross-functional teams and senior SMEs without relying solely on formal authority.
- Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate operational needs into clear program priorities and proposal themes.
- Active Top Secret clearance.

Desired:
- Direct experience with Air Operations Centers, Kessel Run, C3BM, JADC2, CBC2, or related Air Force C2 modernization efforts.
- Experience supporting or interacting with AFLCMC, PAE C3BM, ACC, Kessel Run, AOC weapon system stakeholders, or operational C2 customers.
- Experience with weapon system sustainment, software modernization, operational readiness, performance-based contracting, and contractor performance evaluation.
- Experience supporting proposals, industry engagements, source selections, market research, RFIs, or major acquisition planning activities.
- Master’s degree, JPME, Air War College, or equivalent senior leader development.
- Active TS/SCI

Title:
IT Procurement Manager

The IT Procurement Manager is responsible for leading strategic sourcing, procurement, contract management, and supplier relationship management activities supporting enterprise technology solutions, including software, SaaS applications, cloud services, cybersecurity solutions, hardware, telecommunications, and professional services. This role serves as a strategic business partner to Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Finance, Legal, Enterprise Architecture, Digital Transformation, and business leaders to ensure technology investments deliver maximum value and align with organizational objectives.

The IT Procurement Manager is accountable for developing category strategies, leading complex sourcing initiatives, negotiating enterprise agreements, and managing strategic supplier relationships. Working independently and through a team of procurement professionals, this role drives procurement excellence, supports digital transformation initiatives, identifies continuous improvement opportunities, and ensures compliance with corporate procurement policies and governance requirements. The position also provides leadership, coaching, and oversight to procurement specialists and category management professionals.

The ideal candidate is a strategic procurement leader with extensive experience in technology sourcing, software licensing, cloud services, vendor management, and contract negotiations. The successful candidate combines strong commercial acumen, leadership capability, and technical understanding to optimize technology investments, reduce supplier risk, improve vendor performance, and support enterprise transformation initiatives.

Trinzic is being established as an independent public company through the planned separation of KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business, which is expected to be completed on January 4, 2027. This role offers a rare opportunity to join the organization during a pivotal period of growth and transformation, helping build and support procurement strategies, supplier partnerships, and technology sourcing practices that will position the company for long-term success while supporting critical business and technology initiatives.

jobs.description:
Title:
Director, Marketing

Launching Trinzic
KBR’s Mission Technology Solutions business is expected to spin off in January 2027 and will operate as Trinzic, an independent, publicly traded company with 18,000 employees, a global presence with more than 60 locations, and more than $5 billion in revenue. This is a once-in-a career opportunity to help launch a global brand and create a lasting impression for a modern, tech-forward national security company with customers like NASA, the U.S. Department of War (DoW), and the intelligence community. This position will ultimately become part of that new organization. It’s a unique opportunity to help shape Trinzic’s foundation, built on KBR’s proven track record and resources, and to help build the new company’s vision, culture, and future success.

About the Role
As the Director, Marketing you will lead the strategy, development, and execution of the Trinzic brand across all audiences, channels, and experiences. This role is responsible for defining, elevating, and safeguarding the company's brand identity while driving creative excellence that strengthens market presence, builds engagement, and supports business growth.

Following the launch of the Trinzic name, logo, tagline, and visual identity in July 2026, this leader will play a pivotal role in transforming a newly established brand into a recognized force within the national security and space markets. This is a unique opportunity to shape how customers, employees, investors, and industry partners experience and connect with the Trinzic brand from day one.

We are seeking a strategic brand builder and exceptional storyteller who can translate complex technical capabilities, from astronaut training and space domain awareness to high energy lasers and systems integration, into compelling narratives, impactful campaigns, and distinctive creative experiences. This leader will oversee all brand and creative execution across digital, print, events, executive communications, investor materials, social media, internal communications, advertising, and other corporate assets.

The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in brand strategy and creative leadership gained within a leading agency, Fortune 500 organization, top-tier defense contractor, or similarly complex environment. Success will be measured through brand awareness, audience engagement, employee adoption, campaign performance, and overall contribution to corporate growth objectives.

This role will be based out of the Arlington, VA office and will be a hybrid position.

Key Responsibilities
Brand Strategy & Governance
- Lead the development and execution of the company's global brand strategy, ensuring alignment with business objectives and growth priorities.
- Drive brand adoption across global markets, balancing consistency in messaging and identity with the unique needs of local regions.
- Serve as one of the leaders responsible for establishing, scaling, and protecting the Trinzic brand during its first years as an independent public company.
- Establish and maintain brand governance, standards, guidelines, and approval processes across the organization.
- Drive the evolution of the brand positioning, voice, and value proposition to strengthen market differentiation and awareness.

Creative Leadership & Content Development
- Lead and develop a high-performing creative team, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and excellence.
- Oversee the development of creative assets and campaigns across digital, print, video, social media, events, executive communications, and other marketing channels.
- Ensure creative output reflects brand standards, business objectives, and audience needs.
- Direct creative strategy and execution for major campaigns, launches, internal and customer programs, leadership initiatives, and corporate events.
- Oversee all brand execution and deliverables from graphics, videos, tradeshow booths, PowerPoint presentations, digital brochures, swag, investor relations materials, the company website, newsletters, social media, executive communications, internal intranet sites, advertising, signage, and all other company assets.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement

- Collaborate closely with communications, digital marketing, business development, human resources, and external partners to deliver integrated marketing programs.
- Partner with our People Partners and Talent Acquisition to strengthen employer branding, recruitment marketing, and employee engagement initiatives that enhance Trinzic's ability to attract and retain top talent.
- Present brand strategies, campaign recommendations, and creative concepts to executive leadership.
- Partner with Communications to support reputation management, issues preparedness, and stakeholder communications during critical business events.

Agency & Resource Management
- Lead relationships with external vendors  and production agencies.
- Manage budgets, agency performance, and resource allocation to ensure effective execution and return on investment.
- Evaluate and implement best practices, tools, and processes that enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the creative function.

Insights & Performance Measurement
- Leverage market research, competitive intelligence, and audience insights to inform branding and creative decisions.
- Establish key performance indicators and measurement frameworks to evaluate brand health and campaign effectiveness.
- Monitor performance metrics and recommend optimizations to strengthen engagement, awareness, and business impact.
- Stay informed on emerging marketing, branding, and design trends to continuously advance the organization's capabilities.

Basic Qualifications
Education & Experience
- Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Advertising, Communications, Business, Journalism, Design, or a related field.
- 12+ years of progressive marketing, branding, advertising, or communications experience.
- 5+ years of people leadership experience, including managing, developing, and mentoring creative, marketing, or brand teams in both in-person and remote work environments.

- Experience managing external agencies, creative partners, vendors, and production resources.

- Conduct market assessments, supplier evaluations, and competitive sourcing events to identify best-value solutions.

jobs.title: Global Compensation Director
jobs.description:
Title:
Global Compensation Director

We are KBR
When you become part of our KBR team, your opportunities are endless. Through internal collaboration, and with our partners and customers, we’re defining tomorrow’s challenges, then providing the innovative solutions to overcome those challenges, always maintaining our commitment to Zero Harm and our Sustainability Platform.

In September 2025, we announced that we are spinning our Mission Technology Solutions business into a separate public company. This role would ultimately be part of that new company. Our Mission Technology Solutions business partners with governments and defense, intelligence, space, aviation, and critical infrastructure customers to deliver high-end engineering, science, technology, and mission support solutions. From national security and readiness to advanced research, cyber, logistics, and life-cycle sustainment, our teams help customers solve complex challenges in some of the world’s most demanding environments. Whether supporting operations on the ground, at sea, in the air, or in space, our clients trust us to deliver mission-critical capabilities every day.

Working with us means being rewarded for your contributions. In addition to competitive benefits and professional development, our people are empowered to use all their potential, creating meaningful change for themselves and our clients. We attract the best minds in the world because our expertise thrives on creativity, resourcefulness and collaboration. That is how we supply our clients with cutting-edge solutions.

As the needs of the world change, we’re ready to respond and guide the way forward with strategic, sustainable, and technological advancements grounded in more than a century of practical application and execution.

We Are the People Team
We are strategic partners to the business, shaping the talent, culture, and capabilities that enable sustainable growth and high performance. We operate across global markets, partnering with leaders and teams to design practical, scalable solutions that enhance how work gets done and how people thrive. Through strong business insight, data-driven decision making, and a commitment to continuous improvement, we build talent programs that drive impact at every stage of the organization’s evolution.

About the Role
Reporting to the Vice President, People Operations, the Director, Global Compensation leads the strategy, design, governance, and delivery of global compensation programs across a complex, multi-country environment. This role is accountable for building a globally consistent, market-competitive, and performance-driven compensation framework that supports business objectives, attracts and retains talent, and enhances employee experience.

As the enterprise leader for compensation, you will partner closely with HR, Finance, Talent Acquisition, and business leadership to deliver scalable solutions across base pay, incentive programs, executive compensation, and job architecture. You will balance long-term strategy with operational excellence, ensuring strong governance, market competitiveness, and alignment with broader Total Rewards and business strategies.

About You
Accountability: You take full ownership of the global compensation strategy and delivery. You are accountable for program effectiveness, market competitiveness, internal equity, and governance across all regions.
Collaboration: You build strong partnerships across HR, Finance, Talent Acquisition, and business leadership. You influence effectively across a matrixed global organization to align compensation programs with business priorities.
Analytical Rigor: You use data and insights to inform decision-making. You bring strong analytical capability to compensation design, benchmarking, and program evaluation, ensuring decisions are grounded in data and aligned with market trends.
Enterprise Mindset: You think globally and systemically, ensuring compensation programs are scalable, consistent, and integrated with broader Total Rewards, performance management, and workforce strategies.

Key Responsibilities
- Global Compensation Strategy & Design: Define and lead a comprehensive global compensation strategy, including base pay structures, short- and long-term incentive programs, and executive compensation. Ensure programs are competitive, aligned to business strategy, and support pay-for-performance principles.
- Job Architecture & Pay Structures: Develop and maintain global job architecture, salary structures, and grading frameworks to ensure internal equity, clarity, and scalability across regions and business units.
- Market Benchmarking & Competitive Positioning: Oversee market analysis and benchmarking activities to ensure compensation programs are competitive across global markets. Define compensation positioning strategies aligned with business and talent objectives.
- Incentive & Performance Alignment: Design and manage global incentive programs that align employee performance with business outcomes. Partner with leadership to ensure programs drive desired behaviors and results.
- Vendor & Financial Management: Manage relationships with external compensation survey providers and consultants. Partner with Finance on budget planning, cost analysis, and forecasting related to compensation programs.
- Operational Delivery & Cyclical Processes: Oversee key compensation cycles, including annual merit, bonus planning, salary reviews, and equity programs. Ensure accuracy, efficiency, and a strong employee and manager experience.
- Stakeholder Partnership & Advisory: Act as a trusted advisor to HR and business leaders on compensation strategy, job evaluations, pay decisions, and organizational design. Support mergers, acquisitions, and organizational changes.
- Governance, Compliance & Risk Management: Ensure compliance with all applicable global and local pay regulations, including pay equity, transparency, and reporting requirements. Establish strong governance and controls.
- Compensation Data, Insights & Technology: Leverage data, analytics, and compensation systems to drive insights, support decision-making, and enhance program effectiveness. Partner with HRIS and People Analytics teams.
- Leadership & Team Development: Lead and develop a global compensation team, building capabilities, accountability, and alignment within the broader Total Rewards function.

Basic Qualifications
Education & Experience:
- Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field required.
- 15+ years of progressive experience in compensation or Total Rewards.
- Minimum 5+ years of people leadership experience, including managing teams in a global or regional capacity.
- Experience in a complex, multinational organization preferred.

Functional Expertise & Leadership:
- Deep expertise in global compensation strategy, design, and delivery, including base pay, incentives, and executive compensation.
- Strong understanding of job architecture, market pricing, and pay equity principles.
- Demonstrated experience with compensation benchmarking and survey methodologies.
- Strong financial and analytical acumen, including modeling and cost analysis.
- Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional programs and drive global standardization.
- Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders.
- Experience working with HRIS and compensation management systems (e.g., Workday, SAP) and leveraging data to inform decisions.

Location:
The ideal candidate will be located in the Houston, TX or greater Washington D.C.-Baltimore area. While KBR strives to maintain a global, flexible, diverse, and sustainable work environment for our people, we currently offer flexible working arrangements, including hybrid, remote working, and virtual delivery to help reinforce and strengthen our strong commitment to becoming a more socially sustainable company, allowing us to provide greater work-life balance and flexibility.

Additional Compensation: KBR may offer bonuses, commissions, or other forms of compensation to certain job titles or levels, per internal policy or contractual designation. Additional compensation may be in the form of sign on bonus, relocation benefits, short term incentives, long term incentives, or discretionary payments for exceptional performance.

Title:
Sr. Director, Business Development

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary
KBR’s Exploration & Logistics (E&L) business unit delivers mission-critical solutions supporting global defense, federal civilian, logistics, engineering, and space exploration missions. E&L provides integrated capabilities across logistics and sustainment, mission operations, engineering services, readiness and modernization programs, scientific research support, and exploration initiatives in some of the world’s most complex and challenging environments.

The business unit supports customers across the Department of Defense, federal civilian agencies, and commercial partners, delivering innovative solutions that enhance mission readiness, operational effectiveness, and long-term mission success.

Job Summary
KBR is seeking an experienced Senior Director, Business Development to lead strategic growth initiatives across the Exploration & Logistics portfolio. This position is responsible for identifying, qualifying, shaping, and capturing new business opportunities while developing long-term customer relationships and growth strategies aligned with business objectives.

The successful candidate will partner closely with division leadership, operations teams, solutions architects, and executive leadership to expand KBR’s presence across defense, federal civilian, logistics, engineering, and space exploration markets. This individual will be accountable for pipeline development, capture execution, customer engagement, and achieving growth objectives that support the long-term success of the business unit.

Title:
Procurement Manager

KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets.

KBR is seeking a Procurement Manager to provide strategic leadership for procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier management, contracting, and materials management activities supporting manufacturing operations and major capital investment projects. This role is responsible for developing and executing procurement strategies that ensure equipment, materials, and services are acquired safely, compliantly, on schedule, within budget, and in alignment with quality, operational, and business requirements. The Procurement Manager serves as a key member of the project and business leadership teams, partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, and Project Controls to support the successful delivery of capital projects from concept design through startup and operational readiness. The role establishes procurement governance, oversees strategic supplier relationships, drives commercial excellence, ensures supply chain continuity, and provides leadership on procurement-related risks, opportunities, and performance to support safe, compliant, and successful business outcomes.

Functional job responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Strategic Leadership
- Develop and execute procurement and sourcing strategies supporting manufacturing facilities, operational functions, and capital investment programs.
- Lead procurement functions supporting greenfield, brownfield, expansion, and remediation projects.
- Establish procurement governance, organizational structure, resource planning, reporting, and performance management systems.
- Develop long-range category management and sourcing strategies for critical equipment, process systems, construction services, and operational materials.
- Support organizational growth through supplier innovation, strategic partnerships, and risk mitigation initiatives.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on procurement performance, supplier quality, and cost optimization.

Capital Project Procurement
- Direct procurement activities supporting facility design, construction, startup, and operational readiness.

- Lead sourcing and contracting for process equipment, utilities, manufacturing systems, laboratory equipment, automation systems, construction packages, and engineering services.
- Oversee procurement execution for EPC, EPCM, construction management, design-build, and owner-managed project delivery models.
- Develop procurement execution plans aligned with project schedules and funding commitments.
- Ensure timely delivery of long-lead equipment and critical path materials to support project schedules and operational objectives.
- Lead procurement risk identification and mitigation planning for major capital investments.

Commercial & Contract Management
- Lead commercial negotiations and contract administration activities for strategic suppliers and service providers.
- Negotiate complex agreements including:
- EPC and EPCM contracts
- Construction contracts
- Engineering services agreements
- Process equipment purchases
- Automation and digital systems
- Maintenance and operational support agreements

- Manage contract changes, claims, dispute resolution, and supplier performance throughout project lifecycle execution.
- Collaborate with Legal and Finance to ensure contractual compliance and risk mitigation.

Supplier Quality & Compliance
- Partner with Quality and Supplier Quality organizations to ensure supplier compliance with company requirements and applicable industry standards.
- Support supplier qualification, supplier audits, and quality management programs. •  Monitor supplier quality performance and implement corrective action programs when necessary.
- Develop strategic supplier partnerships that support product quality, operational performance, and supply continuity.

Operational Procurement & Supply Chain
- Support manufacturing and operational activities through strategic sourcing and materials management programs.
- Develop sourcing strategies for direct materials, indirect materials, MRO supplies, critical spare parts, and operational consumables.
- Identify supply chain vulnerabilities and implement contingency plans to ensure uninterrupted operations.
- Lead inventory optimization and supply continuity initiatives for critical materials.

Financial Management
- Accountable for procurement budget performance, savings delivery, cost avoidance initiatives, and working capital improvement.
- Support capital appropriation requests and project business cases through market intelligence and procurement benchmarking.
- Drive total cost of ownership improvements across capital and operational spend categories.
- Deliver measurable value through strategic sourcing and supplier performance initiatives.
