Quality Manager - UZ Islands - Eng. & Procurement – Offshore Water Injection Project

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!
The KBR team of teams delivers future-forward science, technology and engineering solutions and mission-critical services that help governments and companies around the world accomplish their most important objectives, while also helping achieve their sustainability goals. KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design and engineering capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets.
Job Title: Quality Manager - UZ Islands - Eng. & Procurement  – Offshore Water Injection Project
KBR Abu Dhabi is currently seeking an experienced Quality Manager  to join its PMC team supporting a major Offshore Project in the UAE. The role will initially be based in Abu Dhabi , transitioning subsequently to the fabrication yard , and later mobilizing to the offshore site during the execution and commissioning phases.
Job Purpose
The Quality Manager is responsible for establishing, implementing, and managing the Project Quality Management System (QMS) across Engineering and Procurement phases of the Offshore Water Injection Project. The role ensures that all engineering deliverables, procurement activities, vendor-supplied equipment, and project processes comply with ADNOC requirements, contract specifications, international standards, and project quality objectives.
The position provides leadership in quality assurance, quality control, supplier quality management, audits, and continuous improvement to ensure successful project execution and delivery.

Key Responsibilities
Quality Management Leadership
- Develop, implement, and maintain the Project Quality Management Plan (PQMP).
- Establish project quality objectives, KPIs, and performance monitoring systems.
- Lead quality assurance and quality control activities throughout engineering and procurement phases.
- Ensure compliance with contractual, regulatory, and client quality requirements.
- Promote a culture of quality excellence and continual improvement across the project organization.
- Report quality performance to Project Management and Client representatives.

Engineering Quality Assurance
- Establish quality control processes for engineering deliverables.
- Review engineering procedures, standards, and design verification requirements.
- Ensure multidisciplinary engineering deliverables undergo proper reviews and approvals.
- Monitor compliance with project specifications, ADNOC standards, international codes, and regulatory requirements.
- Coordinate design verification, validation, and quality reviews.
- Manage engineering non-conformances and corrective action processes.

Procurement Quality Management
- Develop and implement Supplier Quality Surveillance Plans.
- Ensure procurement activities comply with approved quality requirements.
- Review purchase orders and technical requisitions for quality compliance.
- Monitor supplier performance and quality metrics.
- Participate in technical bid evaluations from a quality perspective.
- Ensure critical equipment and materials meet project specifications and inspection requirements.

Supplier & Vendor Quality Assurance
- Qualify and assess suppliers and manufacturers.
- Conduct supplier audits and capability assessments.
- Review vendors' Quality Plans, Inspection & Test Plans (ITPs), and manufacturing procedures.
- Monitor fabrication quality activities through surveillance and inspections.
- Manage supplier non-conformance reports (NCRs) and corrective actions.
- Coordinate source inspections for critical equipment.

Inspection & Testing
- Develop inspection strategies for major equipment and materials, including: - Water Injection Pump Packages
- Pressure Vessels
- Heat Exchangers
- Piping Materials
- Instrumentation Packages
- Electrical Equipment

- Review ITPs, manufacturing data records, and quality documentation.
- Witness Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT), performance tests, and critical inspections.
- Verify compliance with project quality requirements prior to equipment shipment.

Audit & Compliance
- Develop and execute project audit programs.
- Conduct internal audits, supplier audits, and quality system reviews.
- Support client and third-party audits.
- Track audit findings and ensure timely closure of corrective actions.
- Ensure compliance with ISO 9001 and project quality requirements.

Non-Conformance & Continuous Improvement
- Manage NCR, concession, and deviation approval processes.
- Perform root cause analysis for quality issues.
- Implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
- Analyze quality trends and recommend improvement initiatives.
- Promote lessons learned and best practices across the project.

Documentation & Records Management
- Ensure proper control of quality documentation and records.
- Review Manufacturing Record Books (MRBs) and Vendor Data Books.
- Verify turnover quality documentation completeness.
- Ensure traceability of materials, inspections, and test records.
- Support final project quality dossiers and handover documentation.

Stakeholder Coordination
- Interface with Client Quality representatives, Engineering teams, Procurement, Vendors, and Third-Party Inspection Agencies.
- Support project reviews and management meetings.
- Provide guidance and mentoring to project quality personnel.
- Coordinate quality activities across multiple disciplines and suppliers.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or related technical discipline.
- Lead Auditor Certification (ISO 9001) required.
- ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) or equivalent certification preferred.
- Additional certifications in Quality Management or Supplier Quality are advantageous.

Experience
- 20-25 years of Quality Management experience in the Oil & Gas industry.
- Minimum 8 years in a Quality Management leadership role.
- Extensive experience supporting Engineering and Procurement phases of EPC projects.
- Strong experience with offshore brownfield developments and major equipment procurement.
- ADNOC Offshore project experience highly preferred.
- Proven experience managing supplier quality programs and international vendor networks.

Technical Competencies
Quality Systems
- ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems
- Project Quality Management Plans
- Quality Assurance & Quality Control
- Continuous Improvement Programs
- Risk-Based Quality Management

Procurement & Supplier Quality
- Supplier Qualification & Auditing
- Vendor Surveillance
- Inspection & Test Plans (ITP)
- Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)
- Manufacturing Quality Control
- Material Traceability

Engineering Quality
- Design Verification & Validation
- Technical Compliance Reviews
- Engineering Deliverable Audits
- Management of Non-Conformities
- Root Cause Analysis

Industry Standards
- ISO 9001
- API Standards
- ASME Codes
- ASTM Standards
- NACE Standards
- ADNOC Specifications
- IEC / ISO Standards

Software Skills
- SAP QM
- Intelex
- ETQ Reliance
- Aconex
- AVEVA Engineering
- Power BI
- MS Office Suite

Title:
Corporate Human Resources Generalist

The Corporate Human Resources Generalist supports the day-to-day administration of HR programs, processes, and employee lifecycle activities across Trinzic's corporate functions. Reporting to the Manager, Corporate People Partner, this role serves as a key resource for HR operations, onboarding, recruiting support, employee transactions, and HR systems administration. The position requires strong attention to detail, excellent customer service skills, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment while ensuring compliance with company policies and procedures.

Trinzic is being established as an independent public company through the planned separation of KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business, which is expected to be completed on January 4, 2027. This role offers a unique opportunity to help build foundational people processes and support a growing organization during a significant period of transformation.

Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate and administer employee lifecycle activities, including new hires, promotions, transfers, status changes, and separations.
- Support recruiting and hiring activities by preparing offer letters, processing pre-employment requirements, coordinating background checks and drug screens, and partnering with Talent Acquisition to facilitate candidate onboarding.
- Manage first-day onboarding activities and help ensure a positive and seamless new hire experience.
- Serve as a primary administrator for Workday transactions, maintaining employee records and ensuring data accuracy and integrity.
- Respond to employee and manager inquiries regarding HR policies, procedures, benefits, and employment-related processes.
- Process and audit HR transactions while ensuring compliance with company policies and regulatory requirements.
- Partner with Compensation, Benefits, Talent Acquisition, Mobility, and People Operations teams to support day-to-day HR operations.
- Generate and review workforce reports and HR metrics to support business and People Team needs.
- Assist with the implementation, communication, and administration of HR programs, policies, and initiatives.
- Participate in special projects and operational initiatives associated with Trinzic's growth and evolution as a standalone public company

Basic Qualifications
Education & Experience
- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.
- 2-3+ years of Human Resources, HR Operations, HR Generalist, or Human Resources Coordinator experience
- Experience supporting employee lifecycle activities, onboarding, recruiting coordination, and HR processes within a corporate environment.
- Experience using Workday or another similar enterprise HRIS platform.

Professional Skills & Competencies
- Strong knowledge of HR operations, employee lifecycle processes, and HR compliance requirements.
- Proficiency with Workday or similar HRIS systems.
- Strong organizational, customer service, and communication skills with exceptional attention to detail.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment while handling confidential information with discretion.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and process administration skills.

Preferred Qualifications
- PHR, SPHR, SHRM-CP, or SHRM-SCP certification.
- Experience supporting corporate functions within a public company environment.
- Advanced experience with Workday transactions, reporting, and data management.
- Experience supporting onboarding and employee lifecycle administration at scale.
- Experience supporting organizations during periods of growth, transformation, or organizational change.

jobs.title: Director, People
jobs.description:
Title:
Director, People

At KBR – We do things that matter.
We deliver science, technology and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world. KBR employs approximately 38,000 people worldwide with customers in more than 80 countries and operations in over 29 countries.
KBR is proud to work with its customers across the globe to provide technology, value-added services, and long-term operations and maintenance services to ensure consistent delivery with predictable results. At KBR, We Deliver.
Think.KBR.com

KBR in Australia
With over 65 years working on some of Australia’s largest and most complex projects, KBR has unmatched experience supporting the nation’s critical infrastructure, energy transition and national security priorities. KBR has around 2,000 employees throughout Australia, who are focused on delivering innovative technology and engineering solutions for a safer, more secure and sustainable future.
Learn more about KBR in Australia

Belong, Connect and Grow at KBR
At KBR, we are passionate about our people and our Zero Harm culture. These inform all that we do and are at the heart of our commitment to, and ongoing journey toward being a People First company. That commitment is central to our team of team’s philosophy and fosters an environment where everyone can Belong, Connect and Grow. We Deliver – Together.

The Opportunity:
As Director, People, you will lead the strategic and operational people agenda across the business, ensuring workforce capability, culture, leadership effectiveness and employee experience support the achievement of business objectives. Reporting to the Chief People Officer and serving as a key member of the People Leadership Team, you will partner closely with executive leaders to drive organisational performance, strengthen capability and enable sustainable growth.

This is a rare opportunity to influence the future direction of the People function within a complex and evolving organisation at a pivotal point in its journey. You will lead the development and execution of a contemporary, high-performing people strategy that supports business success while fostering a strong, inclusive culture, playing a critical role during a significant period of transformation.

Following the September 2025, KBR announced the planned separation of its Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) business into a standalone public company. This role will ultimately transition into the new company, providing a unique opportunity to help shape the future workforce, culture and people strategy of an emerging organisation serving government and defence, intelligence, space, aviation and critical infrastructure customers.

This is a permanent full-time opportunity and can be based in Canberra, Brisbane, Melbourne, Sydney or Adelaide.

The successful candidate must hold a Baseline security clearance or higher.

In this role, you will:
- Lead the People strategy and delivery across the business, aligning workforce capability, culture and employee experience with business objectives.
- Partner with executive and senior leaders to translate business priorities into workforce and organisational strategies.
- Lead workforce planning, organisational design, talent management and succession planning initiatives.
- Provide strategic advice on organisational effectiveness, leadership capability, culture and people risk.
- Drive organisational change, transformation and workforce transition initiatives.
- Lead employee and industrial relations strategy, including Enterprise Agreements, workplace relations matters and compliance obligations.
- Champion leadership capability, employee engagement, diversity, inclusion and belonging.
- Ensure compliance with employment legislation, governance frameworks and workforce risk requirements.
- Collaborate with global People leaders to deliver consistent and scalable people solutions.
- Lead, coach and develop a high-performing People team.
- Influence enterprise-wide decision making and build strong partnerships across senior stakeholder groups.
- Champion KBR's Zero Harm culture, promoting a safe, secure and respectful workplace

About You
You are an experienced People executive with a proven track record leading strategic and operational people functions within complex and geographically dispersed organisations. You are a trusted advisor to executive leaders, recognised for your ability to align people strategy with business priorities and deliver sustainable organisational outcomes.

You bring deep expertise across workforce planning, organisational design, employee and industrial relations, organisational change and leadership capability. Commercially astute and outcome focused, you balance business priorities, workforce considerations and risk while providing pragmatic and influential advice on complex people matters.

You are an authentic and collaborative leader who excels in periods of transformation, builds high-performing teams and influences effectively across all levels of an organisation.

To be successful in this role, you will bring:
Essential
- Tertiary qualifications in Human Resources, Employment Relations, Business, Law or a related discipline.
- Significant senior People leadership experience within a complex, geographically dispersed organisation.
- Demonstrated success partnering with executive and senior leadership teams to influence strategic and operational outcomes.
- Proven expertise in workforce planning, organisational design, employee and industrial relations and organisational change.
- Strong knowledge of Australian employment legislation, industrial relations frameworks and compliance requirements.
- Experience developing and implementing People strategies that deliver measurable business outcomes.
- Strong commercial acumen and the ability to balance business priorities, workforce considerations and organisational risk.
- Exceptional stakeholder engagement, influencing and communication skills.
- Demonstrated experience leading and developing high-performing teams.
- Ability to obtain and maintain an Australian Government security clearance

Highly Regarded
- Experience within Defence, Defence Industry, Government or other highly regulated environments.
- Experience supporting large-scale organisational transitions, transformations or restructures.
- Experience leading People functions through significant organisational change.
- Postgraduate qualifications in Human Resources, Business Administration or a related discipline.
- AHRI accreditation or equivalent professional certification.

All candidates will be required to hold and maintain an active Baseline Defence Security Clearance.

What we will offer you:
- A workplace culture certified as a Great Place To Work
- Flexible working
- Competitive salary (including annual reviews)
- Paid parental leave
- Income protection
- Corporate rewards
- Salary packaging/Novated leasing
- Employee stock purchase plans
- Flu shots, skin checks and discounted private health insurance
- Career development: Online learning, mentorship and career pathways

If you’re ready to shape tomorrow, let’s get started. Apply Now!

Please note. Shortlisting will take place as applications are received, therefore the advertisement may close early if a suitable candidate is identified.
As a Major Service Provider of the Australian Defence Force, an AGSVA security clearance will be required and compliance to International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). As such, our hiring decisions are based on the key requirements of each role and candidates are selected based on their unique strengths and experiences.

Notice to Third Parties/Recruitment Agencies: KBR Australia does not accept unsolicited resumes or any liability associated with fees or costs from recruitment agencies, search firms or third parties who have not been engaged directly on this job opportunity. Candidates interested in applying are welcome to submit their application online.

jobs.description:
Title:
Compensation Workday Configuration Analyst

KBR is seeking a Compensation Workday Configuration Analyst to serve as the primary Workday configuration expert supporting Compensation and Advanced Compensation programs. Reporting to the HRIS leadership team, this role is responsible for the design, configuration, testing, optimization, and ongoing support of compensation processes within Workday, including annual merit cycles, bonus planning, equity programs, compensation eligibility frameworks, reporting, and data governance.

The ideal candidate brings deep hands-on experience configuring Workday Advanced Compensation and partnering with Compensation and People teams to translate compensation strategies into scalable system solutions. This role will play a critical part in ensuring the successful administration of annual compensation programs while driving continuous improvement, system integrity, and operational excellence across the Workday platform.

Trinzic is being established as an independent public company through the planned separation of KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business, which is expected to be completed on January 4, 2027. This role offers a rare opportunity to join the organization during a pivotal period of growth and transformation, helping build and support the HR technology, compensation, and people systems capabilities that will position the company for long-term success while serving critical government and commercial missions around the world.

Key Responsibilities
- Serve as the primary configuration expert for Workday Compensation and Advanced Compensation, designing, building, and maintaining compensation plans, eligibility rules, compensation review cycles, bonus plans, equity programs, compensation pools, and related business processes.
- Lead the end-to-end configuration, testing, validation, and execution of annual compensation programs, including merit increases, bonus planning, compensation statements, and salary review processes.
- Configure and maintain compensation frameworks that align with Total Rewards strategies, organizational structures, and business requirements.
- Partner closely with Compensation, Total Rewards, HR, and business stakeholders to translate compensation program requirements into scalable Workday solutions and recommend best practices based on system capabilities.
- Develop, maintain, and enhance Workday compensation reports, dashboards, hubs, and data extracts to support compensation planning, audits, analytics, and decision-making.
- Support compensation-related Workday releases, enhancements, and cycle readiness activities through system testing, user acceptance testing (UAT), validation, and issue resolution.
- Ensure data integrity and compliance through audit controls, validation processes, security configuration, and adherence to data governance standards.
- Troubleshoot and resolve complex compensation system and data issues while providing clear communication and recommendations to stakeholders.
- Plan, coordinate, and execute high-volume data loads utilizing EIBs and other Workday tools to support compensation and broader HR initiatives.
- Provide Tier 2 Workday support and contribute to knowledge management, documentation, training materials, and end-user education
- Support configuration and maintenance activities across Core HCM, Recruiting, Absence, and other Workday functional areas as needed; however, the primary focus of the role remains Compensation and Advanced Compensation.

Basic Qualifications
Education & Experience
- Bachelor's Degree in Human Resources, Information Systems, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field required.
- Workday Pro Certification in Compensation, Advanced Compensation, HCM, or a related Workday module preferred.
- 5+ years of Workday HRIS experience, including at least 3 years of hands-on Workday Compensation and Advanced Compensation configuration experience.
- Demonstrated experience independently configuring and supporting Workday Compensation and Advanced Compensation in a production environment, including annual merit, bonus, incentive, and other compensation planning cycles.
- Must be a U.S. citizen.

Technical & Leadership Skills
- Hands-on expertise configuring Workday Compensation and Advanced Compensation, including compensation cycles, business processes, reporting, and security.
- Strong knowledge of compensation programs and practices, including merit, bonus, incentive, and equity programs.
- Experience delivering scalable Workday solutions and translating business requirements into system configurations.
- Proficiency with Workday reporting tools, calculated fields, and data analysis.
- Experience supporting Workday releases, testing, and production deployments.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred Qualifications
- Workday Pro Certification in Compensation and/or Advanced Compensation.
- Experience supporting global compensation programs and annual compensation review cycles.
- Experience with Compensation Statements, Mass Operation Management, BIRT reporting, and other advanced Workday compensation processes.
- Experience supporting large, complex, or publicly traded organizations.
- Experience across additional Workday functional areas, such as Core HCM, Recruiting, Absence, or Talent.

Location:
The ideal candidate will be located in the Houston, TX or greater Washington D.C.-Baltimore area. While KBR strives to maintain a global, flexible, diverse, and sustainable work environment for our people, we currently offer flexible working arrangements, including hybrid, remote working, and virtual delivery to help reinforce and strengthen our strong commitment to becoming a more socially sustainable company, allowing us to provide greater work-life balance and flexibility.

Additional Compensation: KBR may offer bonuses, commissions, or other forms of compensation to certain job titles or levels, per internal policy or contractual designation. Additional compensation may be in the form of sign on bonus, relocation benefits, short term incentives, long term incentives, or discretionary payments for exceptional performance.
Benefits: KBR offers a selection of competitive lifestyle benefits which could include a 401K plan with company match, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, flexible spending account, disability, paid time off, or flexible work schedule. jobs.description:
Title:
Benefits Analyst

The Programme and Project Partners (PPP) model was mobilised in 2019 with the purpose of transforming major project delivery at the Sellafield nuclear site.
The partnership is delivering a 20-year pipeline of major infrastructure projects to support the decommissioning of Sellafield and to create a clean and safe environment for future generations.
In delivering its pipeline of large-scale infrastructure projects, PPP is creating opportunities for its people, supply chain, economy and communities.
KBR’s rapidly growing nuclear team of teams is working at the forefront of the UK’s nuclear space on some of the most exciting new-build, defence and decommissioning programmes.
KBR was recently named a “Great Place to Work-Certified” company, an honour that underscores the company’s commitment to being a UK employer of choice for people who want to do work that matters.

Due to the nature of our work and security requirements, KBR does not offer sponsorship for this role.  We can only consider applicants with the right to live and work in the United Kingdom
Based in Cumbria or Warrington

The role is responsible for maintaining high-quality benefits data, providing data to support reporting, and providing administrative support to ensure benefits are identified, tracked, realised and communicated effectively.
Working closely with project teams and stakeholders, the successful applicant will ensure the integrity of benefits data, benefits management processes and systems.

- Reconcile and verify data between AMPLIFY and finance.
- Investigate data discrepancies and anomalies, escalating issues to the Benefits Lead with recommendations for resolution.

Data Analysis and Reporting

- Support the benefits lead in development of dashboards and visualisations to support decision-making.
- Configure data findings into clear, concise information suitable for a range of stakeholders.

- Assist project and programme teams in the recording, monitoring, and reporting of benefits.
- Coordinate and facilitate Benefits Review and Touchpoint meetings, including preparation of agendas, reports, and meeting minutes.
- Maintain records, documentation, and audit trails in accordance with governance requirements.
- Ensure stakeholder requirements are met.

Stakeholder Engagement
- Build effective working relationships with project teams and wider stakeholders.
- Provide guidance and support on benefits reporting processes and data requirements.
- Communicate benefits performance information in a professional and accessible manner.
- Support the Benefits Lead in preparing information for governance boards and senior management reviews.

Knowledge Management and Systems
- Manage and maintain the Benefits SharePoint site and associated documentation.
- Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance reporting capabilities, system functionality, and business processes.

Safety and Compliance
- Promote and maintain a positive safety culture consistent with nuclear industry standards.
- Comply with all company procedures, regulatory requirements, and industry standards.
- Work in accordance with the Collaborative Management Plan and all relevant governance arrangements.
- Adhere to all applicable health, safety, security, quality, and environmental requirements.

Principal Accountabilities
- Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and reliability of benefits realisation data and reporting.
- Deliver timely and high-quality benefits analysis, dashboards, and management information.
- Identify and escalate actual or potential risks affecting benefits delivery.
- Maintain governance records, reporting schedules, and supporting documentation.
- Support the Benefits Lead in driving and delivering effective benefits management across the programme portfolio.

Skills and Experience
Essential
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Microsoft Excel skills.
- Experience of Power BI
- Strong data management skills
- Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Strong organisational and administrative capabilities.

Desirable but not essential
- Experience working within the nuclear, engineering, infrastructure, defence, or regulated sectors.
- Knowledge of Benefits Realisation Management

- Experience in data analysis or PMO/benefits management environments.

KBR will provide PMO services, enterprise – level governance, assurance, integration and performance oversight across all projects and programs.

THE ROLE

Reporting to the Project Controls Director, the Senior Risk Manager is responsible provide portfolio-wide risk management services to support effective governance, decision-making, and assurance across the portfolio, in alignment with approved risk policies, frameworks, and systems.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

·       Develop, implement, and administer the approved Risk Management Plan (RMP), including procedures, processes, and templates.
·       Review and supervise Risk Management Plans and risk registers of the PMCs to ensure alignment with the Risk Management Plan.
·       Support the implementation and effective use of risk management systems.
·       Provide guidance and training to PMCs to ensure consistent and effective application of risk management practices.
·       Facilitate Risk meetings and develop Risk Registers for Delivery Programmes and client departments
·       Facilitate mitigation strategies for risks and issues through consolidation of risk registers, meetings, and workshops.
·       Consolidate PMC risk registers into programme-level and departmental risk registers for escalation and reporting.
·       Maintain updated Dashboards for risks and issues across the Portfolio the entire Development.
·       Monthly risk management quality assurance reviews and status updates.
·       Quantitative risk analysis (QRA) of programme-wide strategic, cost, schedule, and advance-warning for risks.
·       Developing cost and schedule contingency assessments at programme and portfolio levels.
·       Supporting Operational Risk Assessments across client departments.
·       Preparation of risk assessment documentation and reports in accordance with Risk Management Plan standards.
·       Key Risk Indicator (KRI) reporting across the Development in alignment with established criteria.

EXPERIENCE, SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE

·       Bachelors degree in engineering, architecture, construction management, business management, or equivalent.

·       Experienced user of MS Office and understanding of project management software for risk reporting.
·       Fluency in English language both written and spoken.

OPNAV N980L is the   Logistics and Readiness Branch of the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations (OPNAV).   It supports the Navy and Marine Corps by analyzing and evaluating aircraft, engines, and support equipment logistics.

Role and Responsibilities:
- Support the Requirements Officer during all phases of the Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System (JCIDS) process. This includes technical writing, preparation, or review of formal requirements documents such as: concepts of operations, capabilities-based assessments, analysis of alternatives, initial capabilities documents, capabilities development documents, and requirements memoranda.

- Provide analysis on Future Year’s Defense Program (FYDP) and year of execution requirements vetting to ensure the Fleet’s top priorities are supported and defended.

- Route draft program-related documents and incorporate salient comments into final versions.

- Research, investigate, and evaluate program requirements, resourcing, and objectives in the annual Program Objectives Memorandum (POM) process.

- Conduct studies and provide results to the Government pertaining to evaluation and analysis of program performance; research aviation development trends as it applies to associated programs.

- Conduct investigative analysis to assess the impact of programmatic changes on system(s) acquisition, support, and sustainment.

- Provide analysis of technology advancements, as well as product and/or process improvements to increase warfighter capabilities and performance.

- Analyze and review similar programs led by other Services and Agencies to leverage Joint applications.

- Provide technical analysis support and understanding of program requirements to the Fleet (Naval Aviation Requirements Group (NARG), Enabler NARG (ENARG), TYCOM Priority Panel (TPP), Operational Advisory Group (OAG), Users Conference, etc.) and other NAVAIR Program Managers (PMs), SYSCOMs, and Joint Services for existing and arising products and capabilities.

- Support the prioritization and incorporation of Fleet-generated requirements (NARG, ENARG, TPP, OAG, Users Conference, etc.) to develop the Program Requirements Review (PRR) brief to OPNAV N98 to include justification and issue sheets.

- Provide support in the generation or analysis of weapon system master plans, which directly feed Type Model Series (T/M/S) Platform Capability Evolution Plans, to document and plan for future capabilities.

- Provide technical writing for the government in response to related Navy internal, Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), and Congressional taskers. Draft the response for government review and final submission.

Liaison
- Interface with NAVAIR Program Office Assistant Program Managers for Logistics (APML) and Business Financial Managers (BFMs), OPNAV Resource Sponsors and Requirements Officers, Office of Financial Management and Budget (FMB) analysts, and Naval Supply System Command financial and logistics managers to gather information and help promote well-researched decisions.

- Work closely with NAVAIR Business Operations Group, and Commander Fleet Readiness Centers to assist in depot maintenance requirements development, recommend resourcing decisions and outlining risk based upon available funds.

- Ensure coordination of depot maintenance requirements with entities outside of the Air Warfare Division (OPNAV N98) to include OSD CAPE, HQMC Aviation, and NAVAIR offices.

- Maintain liaison with other OPNAV N-codes with naval aviation maintenance equity to ensure data validity/sufficiency for the lead Requirements Officer to develop and defend depot maintenance requirements and budgets.

Programming/Budgetary Execution:
- Monitor the Program Budget Information System (PBIS) for changes and construct load sheets as needed in support of budget programming.

- Build government approved POM issue sheets to define program needs or budgetary shortfalls.

- Review program budget decisions (PBD), or resource management decisions, Fact-of- Life Change Proposals, and corporate bills and assess their impacts on aviation maintenance requirements and associated enabler accounts.

- Provide assistance to Program Offices, COMFRC, and/or NAVAIR Sustainment and Business Operations Groups on budget exhibit preparation and review submissions for anomalies that could result in punitive marks.

- Provide financial management support by monitoring programmed and budgeted resources against actual execution of approved funds.

- Identify issues, concerns, and impact of budgetary adjustments to ensure funds are effectively and efficiently meeting Department of the Navy (DoN) needs.

Subject Matter Expert:
- Serve as the focal point for continuity and as the principal advisor to N98 leadership for aviation maintenance programs, including aviation depot (airframes, engines, support or components) and intermediate levels of maintenance.

- Provide analysis or advocacy of aviation maintenance policy issues through participation in related strategic development sessions (Integrated Project/Cross Functional Teams, special advisory boards, or working groups), or via preparation of guidance and facilitation of policy execution.

- Perform studies and provide information that contributes to the Government’s knowledge of aviation maintenance, including but not limited to examining repair turn-around-time, workload standards, and their inter-relationships.

Title:
Project Procurement Manager

KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets.

KBR is looking for a Project Procurement Manager (PPM) is responsible for leading all procurement and materials management activities for a large-scale capital project within an Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) environment. This role ensures timely, cost-effective, compliant acquisition of engineered equipment, bulk materials, and subcontracted services in alignment with project schedules, budgets, contractual obligations, and applicable regulatory requirements—including Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS) and Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) where applicable.

The PPM serves as the primary procurement interface for the project, working closely with Project Management, Engineering, Construction, Contracts, Legal, and Government Compliance teams, as well as suppliers and subcontractors.

Functional job responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Procurement Planning & Strategy
- Develop and execute the Project Procurement Execution Plan, aligned with contract requirements, project schedule, and sourcing strategy.
- Establish procurement strategies for engineered equipment, bulk materials, construction services, and long-lead items.
- Identify procurement risks, including regulatory, supply chain, and schedule risks, and implement mitigation plans.

Supplier Management & Contracting
- Lead supplier prequalification, bid strategy development, solicitation, evaluation, and award recommendations.
- Negotiate commercial terms and conditions in compliance with client contracts, company policies, FAR, DFAR, and flow-down requirements.
- Ensure suppliers and subcontractors comply with DPAS ratings, priority delivery requirements, and government-mandated schedules.
- Resolve commercial issues, claims, and performance disputes in coordination with Contracts and Legal.

Schedule, Cost & Risk Control
- Ensure procurement activities support the project critical path and overall execution schedule.
- Monitor committed, forecast, and actual procurement costs against the approved project budget.
- Identify cost-saving and value-engineering opportunities while maintaining regulatory and contractual compliance.
- Track procurement-related risks, expediting actions, and mitigation measures.

Materials Management & Logistics
- Coordinate with expediting, inspection, materials management, and logistics teams to ensure timely fabrication, inspection, and delivery.
- Ensure compliance with DPAS priority requirements for shipping, allocation, and delivery sequencing.
- Support site materials management, inventory control, and surplus disposition in accordance with contract requirements.

Cross-Functional Coordination
- Interface with Engineering to align technical specifications, vendor data requirements, and compliance documentation.
- Support Construction by ensuring timely availability of materials and services and resolution of field procurement issues.
- Collaborate with Project Controls on forecasting, progress measurement, and procurement status reporting.

Compliance & Governance
- Ensure procurement activities comply with: - Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) (DFAR)
- Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS)
- Client-specific government contract clauses and flow-down requirements
- Company ethics, quality, safety, and sustainability policies

- Maintain accurate, audit-ready procurement documentation suitable for government and internal audits.
- Support compliance reporting and audits related to government-funded projects.

Team Leadership
- Lead, mentor, and manage project procurement staff, including buyers, expeditors, and materials coordinators.
- Assign responsibilities, establish performance expectations, and provide day-to-day decision support.
- Promote disciplined procurement execution and compliance awareness across the project team.

Required Education, Experience, & Skills:
- Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, or a related field
- Master’s degree or professional certifications (e.g., CPSM, CIPS, PMP) preferred
- 10–15+ years of procurement or supply chain experience in an EPC or large capital project environment
- Proven experience managing procurement for large, complex capital projects, preferably with government or defense-related funding
- Demonstrated experience with: - Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), including flow-down clauses and subcontract compliance
- Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS) requirements, including rated orders and priority fulfillment

- Strong background in procurement of engineered equipment, bulk materials, and construction services
- Experience working with domestic and international suppliers and complex logistics environments

Skills & Competencies
- Strong commercial negotiation and contract management skills
- Working knowledge of government contracting compliance requirements
- Ability to balance cost, schedule, quality, and regulatory obligations
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities
- Proficiency with ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle) and procurement tracking tools
- Leadership capability in fast-paced, schedule-driven project environments

Working Conditions
- Project-based role with potential for extended hours during critical milestones

jobs.title: Risk Manager
jobs.description:
Title:
Risk Manager

The Programme and Project Partners (PPP) model was mobilised in 2019 with the purpose of transforming major project delivery at the Sellafield nuclear site.
The partnership is delivering a 20-year pipeline of major infrastructure projects to support the decommissioning of Sellafield and to create a clean and safe environment for future generations.
In delivering its pipeline of large-scale infrastructure projects, PPP is creating opportunities for its people, supply chain, economy and communities.
KBR’s rapidly growing nuclear team of teams is working at the forefront of the UK’s nuclear space on some of the most exciting new-build, defence and decommissioning programmes.
KBR was recently named a “Great Place to Work-Certified” company, an honour that underscores the company’s commitment to being a UK employer of choice for people who want to do work that matters.
Due to the nature of our work and security requirements, KBR does not offer sponsorship for this role.  We can only consider applicants with the right to live and work in the United Kingdom

RISK MANAGER
Purpose - Responsible for implementing and maintaining effective risk management arrangements for the project, ensuring risks are identified, assessed, managed and reported to support successful project delivery.

Key Responsibilities
- Prepare the Project Risk Management Plan with the Project Manager.
- Implement and maintain project risk management systems and tools.
- Support Risk Owners in managing and maintaining the project risk register.
- Conduct quantitative risk analysis and provide risk-based insights.
- Facilitate risk reviews and workshops, including Gateway stage reviews.
- Ensure project risk data is accurate, current and complete.
- Support suppliers in the identification, assessment and treatment of risks.
- Report lessons learned and risk management findings to the PPP Programme Risk Manager.
- Manage the workload and development of the Project Risk Practitioner.
- Provide risk reports and advice to the Project Manager and project stakeholders as required.

Skills and Experience
- Experience in project or programme risk management.
- Knowledge of risk management methodologies and tools.
- Experience facilitating workshops and stakeholder engagement.
- Strong analytical, communication and reporting skills.
- Ability to influence and support effective decision-making across project teams.

Reporting Line - Reports to the relevant Project Manager in accordance with the project's Risk Management Plan. Maintains a functional relationship with the PPP Programme Risk Manager.

The role is based in Warrington and you would be working in the office 3 days a week so would need to be with an easy commute of Warrington.
#LI-JI1

jobs.title: Risk Analyst
jobs.description:
Title:
Risk Analyst

1.1 Purpose:
To support the implementation and maintenance of project and enterprise risk management (ERM) processes across engineering and project delivery assignments. The Risk Analyst is responsible for maintaining project risk registers, facilitating risk identification and assessment activities, monitoring mitigation actions, and providing accurate risk reporting to support informed decision-making and successful project delivery.
1.2 Key Responsibilities:
- Support the implementation of project and enterprise risk management processes across assigned projects.
- Maintain and update project risk and opportunity registers, ensuring information remains accurate, current, and auditable.
- Assist in facilitating risk identification workshops and risk review meetings with project teams and stakeholders.
- Develop structured risk statements and support qualitative risk assessments using approved methodologies.
- Monitor risk mitigation actions and follow up with risk owners to ensure timely closure of actions.
- Track emerging risks and opportunities throughout the project lifecycle and escalate significant issues where required.
- Support the evaluation of schedule, cost, technical, commercial, procurement, and execution risks.
- Prepare risk reports, dashboards, heat maps, and management presentations.
- Coordinate risk data collection and maintain consistency across risk management systems and reporting tools.
- Support Project Managers, Project Controls, Engineering Leads, and Commercial teams in risk-related activities.
- Assist with contingency planning and the development of mitigation strategies.
- Ensure risk management activities align with project governance requirements and company procedures.
- Support lessons learned reviews and ensure risk-related knowledge is captured for future projects.

1.3 Deliverables:
- Project Risk Registers
- Opportunity Registers
- Risk Action and Mitigation Tracking Logs
- Monthly Risk Reports and Dashboards
- Risk Heat Maps and Risk Matrices
- Risk Workshop Records and Action Logs
- Management Risk Review Presentations
- Emerging Risk Reports
- Lessons Learned and Risk Closure Reports
- Project Risk Status Updates for Governance Reviews

1.4 Compliance & Standards:
- Company Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Framework.
- Project Risk Management Plans (RMPs).
- Client project risk management requirements and procedures.
- ISO 31000 Risk Management Principles and Guidelines.
- Company governance, assurance, and reporting requirements.
- Project Controls and Risk Management best practices applicable to engineering and project delivery environments.

1.5 Qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering (any discipline), Construction Management, Project Management, or a related field.
- Minimum 2-3 years of experience in project support, project controls, planning, document control, junior engineering, or risk management roles within engineering and project delivery organizations.
- Experience within oil & gas, energy, infrastructure, or industrial projects preferred.
- Basic understanding of risk management principles, including risk identification, assessment, mitigation, monitoring, and reporting.
- Familiarity with Project Risk Management Plans (RMPs) and structured risk registers.
- Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office applications.
- Strong written English skills with the ability to prepare clear and concise risk statements and reports.
- Familiarity with engineering project lifecycles, particularly Pre-FEED, FEED, and Detailed Design phases.
- Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and stakeholder coordination skills.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks while maintaining accuracy, attention to detail, and data integrity.
